scope_from_suite_docstring: Compare callable adaptive/burst spark slices with stock BMHM instructions.  Only CB15 is stubbed at the slot6 boundary; its successful return and selected input changes are explicit fixtures. This does not implement CB15 or A466.

Foreground self-copy, virtual-stack watermark and startup timer joins.  Logical stack bytes are observed as data. WAI/RTI and native C stack layout remain explicit target boundaries; no ordinary ISR is delivered while masked.

Compare board flush, MAP/VSS/brake input and housekeeping with actual BMHM.  The11-cycle delay is an explicit backend boundary. Intervening callback effects and sequential controller joins do not establish a target ABI or physical pins.

Controller boot entries and real callee joins versus recorded stock BMHM.  Data tracing retains logical operand width/order and excludes private HC11 stack traffic. Previously ported native callees contribute their actual state, not fabricated address-space events for their native C field operations.

Focused retained-boot C/ROM comparisons, including the rooted full checksum.  Foreign operand transactions are recorded separately from instruction fetch and private HC11 stack traffic. This does not establish a native target ABI.
Compare $7C13 and its $3068 handoff with BMHM, retaining state over three ticks.
Resident EGR PI/duty publication, with actual feedback and output joins.
Actual EGR demand/fraction, resident controller joins and fuel/spark consumers.  Optional1815 is a visible host callback fixture, not invented module code.

Recurring factory qualification/upload/callback/output paths versus BMHM.  FA5B's abandoned-frame precondition and FAA5's unknown target are explicit supplied test bindings. Trap stops before SWI; wait stops at FBD4. No physical interrupt or arbitrary supplied callback implementation is inferred.

TPS, CTS/MAT/BARO and VE/air-charge C versus hash-checked BMHM instructions.  Producer/consumer joins are explicit calls, not a claim that the broad fuel and slot1/4/D/F roots or target interrupt timing are implemented.

Resident7D4B controller, ignition, governor and scheduled tail versus BMHM.  Previously checked native slices contribute real state and I/O. Newly ported logical routines also compare RAM/calibration operand transactions.

Independent full BMHM ROM replay for complete $7D4B..$8547 entry.  This deliberately starts from the stock ROM entry rather than hand-joining callee fragments. It first checks bounded no-fuel and ignition transitions; other running/async and physical output histories remain separate evidence. The 0x4000..FFFF bytes come from SHA-checked committed full-ROM evidence.

Cut/decel, reservoirs and connected crank/running delivery against BMHM.  The broad ignition/admission prefix and852C scheduled tail stay separate. Typed bus fixtures do not establish physical injector/ASIC timing or delivered fuel.

O2/BLM state machines and pulse-correction C versus hash-checked BMHM.  The complete running admission/cut/decel/async path and physical response remain separate. Explicit test joins do not skip those stages in the production root.

Independent BMHM HC11/C differential for the entire governor target.  Runs on the repository's recorded SHA256-identified ROM evidence, not HAC comments. It compares selected native RAM and $306C output bytes after each callee. Target stacks/interrupt latency and the optional $1809 interface remain separate, explicit boundaries. Never claim physical governor testing.

BMHM $7D4B..$7DB5 C versus executed HC11, including stop/trap boundaries.  Use ROM bytes from the committed SHA-identified upstream evidence, not the provisional HAC comments or guessed calibration. No live target ABI.

Narrow, deterministic RAM-owner gate for literal factory FUEL writes.  This is not a whole-ROM, indexed/pointer, or target hardware completeness test. It only covers CPU addresses directly listed as WRITE operands in the maintained source-scoped factory_fuel_memory_accesses.csv.

Crank admission, startup/AE and commanded AFR/PE against hash-checked BMHM.  Hardware callbacks are supplied fixtures; extension1800 and the BLM/tail joins remain explicit. The running fuel root is not replaced by these callable stages.

ADC/battery and injector-finalizer C versus actual stock BMHM instructions.  ADC completion and callbacks are supplied bus fixtures, not an electrical model. The fuel tail at852C and slot-F work afterE306 remain outside these slices.
Compare compiled C fuel arithmetic with actual stock instruction execution.
Replay whole BMHM slots 03 and 0B, with focused witnesses for their shared helpers.

Compare compiled C startup/REF transactions with bounded stock execution.  Peripheral readbacks are explicit fixture inputs. This checks transaction width, order, values and the REF latch; it does not model device timing or physical I/O.

Source-only proof of safe optional native-C startup in the ASM11 master.  Assembler output/link address, true MC68HC11 compiler ABI and target RAM need independent verification; this test does not establish any of them.

Fail-closed ASM11 native ISR entry source contract.  This is not a binary/ABI proof. It enforces safety properties of the maintainable ASM11 ROM source until an actual linked compiler RTS thunk and S19/ROM tests exist.

Check C vector provenance against stock BMHM and both existing ASM11 images. The current ROM intentionally traps every interrupt except reset. This is source validation, NOT a native compiler ABI or assembled BIN proof.
Fast source-only gate; does not establish ROM-wide or target equivalence.

Compare resident desired RPM/background IAC and their caller with stock BMHM.  Only unsupplied180C/180F/1812 and the not-yet-ported ACA7 use return fixtures. Mode12 supplies a subsequent normal phase8 call, not the intervening input work.

Compare the resident main IAC and its callees with actual BMHM instructions.  1803/180F/1812 use named well-formed return fixtures, never a guessed machine ABI. Joined calls supply their own admissions and do not synthesize acquisition or steps.

Compare slot9, follower and slow-IAC C routines with actual stock instructions.  EGR CF16 and VSS D4DA remain explicit return fixtures. Joined calls supply later phase/input admissions; they do not replace the intervening input pipeline.

Check the resident IAC step/count service and selected sequential joins.  Literal mask assignments are observable boundaries; callback effects are fixtures, not a target interrupt ABI or a guarantee that every count reaches the motor.

Resident reset/trap/fallback/XIRQ leaves, including factory REF completion.  Normal hardware frame entry/RTI and terminal reset/loop transfers stay explicit. XIRQ exposes its supplied saved-CCR byte as an ordered logical data access.

Check decay, the mux/ADC diagnostic and normal KR against stock instructions.  The IRQ witnesses use explicit logical mask boundaries. Points 1 and 2 are one-shot admission attempts; a masked attempt is deliberately consumed. Point 3 holds a post-unmask request until the CPU admits it, including the architectural one-instruction delay after CLI. These fixtures do not establish physical knock, ADC settling, hardware IRQ level/flag behavior, arbitration, or a native C mask backend's instruction boundaries.

Compare OC1's compiled C with actual stock interrupt entry/body/RTI.  Counter samples are coherent fixture words, not a physical knock device model. Calibration variants change only the selected direct-index table entries.

Actual BMHM OC5/OC4 instructions versus the vector-dispatched C bodies.  The factory side fetches both complete handlers from hash-identified committed bytes, enters through the CPU interrupt API, and executes RTI. No handler or callee is replaced. PORTA/TCNT samples and W1C are explicit fixture premises; this is not a timer-edge model, native C ABI test, or cycle-accuracy claim. The CPU implementation is the independently audited legacy interpreter, not a second independent emulator. Literal witnesses and RAM access checks below also constrain its result rather than trusting C/ROM agreement alone.

Differential execution of the complete resident REF handler and its callees.  Inputs provide RAM, calibration variants and explicit peripheral samples. CPU entry/RTI is real on the ROM side; C ABI, physical timing and ASIC semantics remain target work. Timer words are a supplied sequence, not a hardware model.

scope_from_suite_docstring: Compare six input/consumer groups and scheduled joins with actual stock BMHM.  Historical suites keep isolated boundary fixtures. This suite links the resident AC, VSS and shift-lamp bodies. Optional modules and CF16 remain explicit returns.

SCI transport/session and boot slices against recorded BMHM instructions.  Coherent logical-address bindings and supplied SCI status are host fixtures. Target interrupt frames, controller-service execution and physical bus timing remain separate work. Invalid descriptor cycles have a C-only bounded guard.

Retained service lifecycle/clear footprints versus actual BMHM bytes.  The AE85..AE9C eight-callee prefix remains a supplied dependency. Native RAM owners and foreign byte accesses are distinguished explicitly in this fixture. This is not a target memory-placement or interrupt-timing proof.

Compare BMHM shift observation, adaptation and long-shift diagnosis with C. Replay the parent and individual stages, comparing ordered stores, cell/checksum critical sections and retained bytes through $032B, including failure prefixes.

Compare C514 output, F5DC probe and ordered slot7 publication with BMHM.  180C, 9E99 and ACA7 returns are explicit dependency fixtures. Mode3 supplies a subsequent normal spark call at phase8; it does not replace intervening factory input work, prove physical output behavior or reconstruct module machine ABIs.
Run both groups of scheduler slot 04 and compare with the stock HC11 entry.
SlotF diagnostic prefix and complete output/fault/fuel/REF joins versus BMHM.
Compare scheduler slots 05 and 0A with the recorded BMHM instructions.
Replay the two final slow slots from their stock BMHM scheduler entries.
Slot1, callable slotF suffix and slow fuel producers versus actual BMHM.  The preceding C514/C4F5 slotF group remains an explicit caller precondition.
Check routine/file ownership and the ROM anchors behind the initial outline.

Compare the A466..A5E4 prelude against stock BMHM instructions.  AC51 is an explicit dependency fixture. Stop before the first SWI at A5D7; the trap frame/handler/loop and A5E5 period/RPM continuation are outside scope.

Check resident override, signed limits and post-limit service against BMHM.  1812 remains unknown. Active extension witnesses stop at its entry or use an explicit fixture return/state effect; they do not reconstruct the module ABI.

Check the EST monitor and complete resident A466..ACA6 controller.  This binary links the production alternate adapter. Only 180F/1812 returns are fixtures; timeout execution stops before SWI. Word transaction ordering is a host contract, not proof of physical EST timing or module machine ABIs.

Compare idle, transient and decel spark with actual stock instructions.  Optional feature/calibration variants are fixture data, not changes to the truck image. Full-composite witnesses end before external1812 and later limits.

Compare AB44..ABCA output and AC51..ACA6 alternate RPM against BMHM.  Normal joined cases stop before the ABCB monitor. 180F/1812 returns are explicit fixtures, not supplied module implementations or reconstructed machine ABIs.

Check normal period/RPM preparation and joined command building against BMHM.  AC51/1812 effects are explicit dependency fixtures. Stop before SWI or AB44; neither a trap handler nor physical EST output is implemented by these tests.

Compiled-C comparison with base/environmental spark and shared math ROM.  Calibration variants preserve each source table's bounded storage. A separate 527-byte matrix fixture exercises arbitrary byte strides and row-product wrap.

Complete C668..C6BA speed-source versus stock BMHM HC11 instructions.  The stock ROM is taken from SHA-identified full 0x4000..FFFF evidence; synthetic RAM and cases are test-only. Stop at original RTS to 0x7000.

Working-RAM reset and literal clear helper versus recorded BMHM instructions.  The provider binds selected existing named owners. Stack/cycle and physical RAM backing remain target contracts; the digest covers the complete fixture image.

Initial ADC sampling, partial factory admission and timer prefix versus BMHM.  The factory timer slice stops before FA5B's target SP assignment. Ready-state, input muxing and selected callback mutations are explicit peripheral fixtures.

Independent ADAA..AE5B electronic/non-electronic TCC ROM differential.  The source is the hash-recorded full BMHM ROM, not the HAC labels. Current test is logic/RAM equivalence, not physical TCC-solenoid behavior.

Compare captured-X guard policy to actual795C..7976 stock instructions.  The existing host contract sweeps every X. Default ROM comparison does too; --focused keeps development runs to boundaries, byte-class representatives, callback mutation and each access-failure prefix. LDS/entry remain explicit.

Differential of stock BMHM D4EB diagnostics with actual HC11 execution.  Four entry contexts: E684, E6AC, E69C complete RTS and the contiguous D4EB..D4F7 prefix. The 9-entry E6BC mask loops are executed, not replaced by HAC label text. The later D4F7..D69E gear decision is OUT OF SCOPE and must not be silently treated as implemented.

Independent BMHM D5B7..D69E candidate-gear selection C/HC11 differential.  Input is accumulator-B (candidate) at the exact D5B7 instruction boundary. The gear-slot differential covers its D4F7..D5B6 caller through both scheduled entries. The original E562 callee is executed in ROM, including indexed reads beyond the nominal range table. No hardware transmission actuator is exercised.

Stock HC11 $E562..$E57B ROM differential for proposed gear limiter.  The lookup is deliberately allowed to index beyond the nominal 4-byte tables: this is what the original indexed X arithmetic actually does.
BMHM $B334 movement and $E654 reaction mask against their C entry points.
Compare the final $C4E5 callee at $C40A against the original BMHM instructions.

Run the five factory callees at $C4E5 in order, plus isolated mode/range/shift entries. Compare retained RAM and ordered provider writes, including failed prefixes. The shared HC11 interpreter uses logical RAM and calibrated ROM tables.
ROM HC11 $D8CE carry-qualified multi-pointer table differential.  D8CE is tested independently of its D4EB caller using the caller's X table and B entry value. Carry is reflected as the `valid` flag.

HC11 bit branches: all selected set/clear, including an empty mask.  Authority: NXP M68HC11ERG rev2.1 p12, Bit Manipulation Branches: https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/reference-manual/M68HC11ERG.pdf This is an instruction-semantic check, not a bus/cycle timing proof.

Unsigned HC11 indexed operands, distinct from signed relative branches.  Primary authority: NXP AN1283 section5.1.2: https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/application-note/AN1283.pdf These are CPU operand/address checks, not device or instruction timing proofs.
Native build driver demands actual compiler and explicit placement.
Fail-closed composition tests; synthetic bytes are NOT a firmware proof.
Native C linker placement contract tests. No C cross compiler required.
Native ASM11/C boot binding; synthetic machine bytes only.
MC68HC11 ELF layout validation using synthetic objdump/nm evidence.
Static ABI-probe sanity; does not pretend a native compiler is installed.

Independent negative tests for native artifacts and HC11 bus apertures.  Set AUDIT_REPO to a baseline checkout to demonstrate the pre-fix failures. All code bytes here are synthetic; these tests do not qualify firmware.
Executable comparator tests; synthetic BINs are not firmware validation.

Census safeguards, not firmware-equivalence tests.  Run: python -m unittest discover -s tests/audit -p test_equivalence_inventory.py -v Negative tests deliberately remove evidence or inflate a classification and assert the audit rejects that change. The separate --require-complete gate is expected to fail on the audited development snapshot.

Manual-derived HC11 conformance tests, independent of either decoder.  Run: python tests/audit/test_hc11_isa.py [--repo CHECKOUT] [--matrix OUT.json] AUDIT_REPO is an equivalent checkout selector. No BIN or third-party packages are needed. The test oracle never imports production flag/address helpers.
XIRQ must not be hidden behind a pending maskable IRQ in the coordinator.

Source-bound output-timer saturation checks for the HC11 16-bit-int ABI.  The actual pulse declaration, conditional += and width initializer are parsed from output_timer_internal.h. A bounded C integer-semantics model evaluates them; independent arithmetic and literal witnesses supply expected results. This is not native HC11 execution, timing or whole-handler verification.  Run: python -m unittest discover -s tests/audit -p test_output_timer_arithmetic.py -v AUDIT_REPO may select another checkout containing the output-timer helper. This new suite is deliberately separate from the pinned preimplementation baseline's original 14-method arithmetic suite.

Executable source-bound regressions for 16-bit int arithmetic.  Run: python -m unittest discover -s tests/audit -p test_target_arithmetic.py -v Set AUDIT_REPO=/absolute/path to test the unmodified development checkout. These tests model C expression widths; they do NOT execute native HC11 code.
Definition semantics and reversible in-memory edits; never create a BIN.

Bounded actual-ROM checks of high-impact documentation reductions.  No full transmission/device simulation is asserted. Fixtures explicitly set RAM and counterfactual calibration bytes where a branch boundary is tested. The runner retains its historical all-or-none multi-bit BRSET input domain. The general CPU now implements all-selected semantics; its separate exhaustive byte/mask regression and new IAC tests cover partial-mask cases.

Resident interrupt nesting, X snapshots and current-loop ordering in BMHM.  All selected handler instructions and resident callees execute. Arrival times, ready/status bits and flat device samples are supplied inputs, not a model of the actual timer/ADC/bus. The historical guarded replay retains its zero/full-mask BRSET witness domain; separate CPU tests now verify all selected-bit patterns.

Selected stock-BMHM interrupt contracts needed by an independent rewrite.  No CPU or peripheral simulator is changed. Device words are flat coherent fixture samples; SCI ready/error bits and arrivals are explicitly supplied. Scheduler-only tests retain the existing runner's explicit callee stubs. These witnesses prove selected schedules, not arbitrary timing or interleavings.

Join real stock handlers to source flags, priority and nominal time.  Instruction-end timer writes avoid equality/inhibition border claims. ASIC words remain explicit samples. The counter drives admission; no IRQ is inserted at a selected current-calculation instruction.

Joined stock service/mode transitions and explicit optional-code fixtures.  All resident instructions are stock BMHM. Supplied RAM handlers are tiny test programs, never claims about the absent GM module. ASIC values and IRQ times are fixture inputs; caller fragments have explicit start/stop boundaries.

Execute selected factory masked intervals and complete REF/SCI handlers.  Nominal instruction costs are independent of the CPU core's accounting. Peripheral samples and interrupt arrivals remain supplied test inputs.

Stack envelopes and complete-handler shared-output witnesses for stock BMHM.  No hardware-timing claim: ADC ready values and IRQ arrivals are fixture inputs. The IAC/gear witness executes all resident callees of the selected TOC3 passes. The historical all-or-none BRSET fixture domain remains explicit. The CPU's all-selected branch semantics are now independently tested over all byte/mask pairs; partial-mask IAC comparisons are supplied by the newer source suite.

Cross-routine factory REF/startup/EST checks using the unchanged BMHM bytes.  The peripheral fixture provides stationary coherent words, not an ASIC model. Actual REF IRQ entry/RTI and the full A4EC..ACA6 calculation are executed. These are bounded schedules and chosen inputs, not all-interleaving proofs.
Regression checks for data/code confusion and exact direct access indexing.

Conditional timing of complete stock BMHM busy timer handlers.  The independent timing subset, F1-style divide-by16 compare, ADC completion and CLI delay supply an explicitly scoped test environment. Register writes commit at instruction endpoints; cases avoid compare-write equality borders. There is no competing-source, bus-stretch, watchdog, STOP or reset model.

Manual-idle strategy against native C and actual HC11 instructions.  The default fixture contains recorded Rev A excerpts, never a bootable BIN. Tests establish software behavior, not engine stability or target readiness.
Rev B gate tests execute emitted HC11, with exact Rev A reference excerpts.
Reader coverage and safety of local explanatory flag/pointer provenance.
Check functional grouping, fixed-operand scope and recorded context anchors.
